correctness.rationale: The chain-ring valuation decomposition gives \(|V_i|=(q-1)q^{\ell-i-1}\) and adjacency exactly when \(i+j\ge\ell\). In the simple graph, degrees are \(q^i-1\) or \(q^i-2\) according to whether self-annihilation occurs, and these degrees strictly separate layers. Hence every layer permutation is independent and all automorphisms are their product. Twin classes force all but one vertex per layer in determining/resolving sets; the proposed witness in \(V_{\ell-j}\) distinguishes omitted representatives from distinct layers. The \(\ell=2\) boundary agrees with the complete-graph formula.

originality.rationale: Rattanakangwanwong--Meemark already prove for arbitrary finite chain rings that the unit orbits are exactly \(R^\times\theta^i\), give their sizes \((q-1)q^{\ell-i-1}\), and prove the orbit-level adjacency threshold \(i+j\ge\ell\); their reduction graph is therefore the same valuation-layer blow-up, up to the paper's loop convention. Once this complete graph structure is known, the product automorphism group and determining number follow immediately from distinct layers and twins, while the metric-dimension upper witness is a short routine check. Sabeel--Paramasivam independently show the same twin/generalized-join method for \(\mathbb Z_n\). Under the implication-based originality rule, the combined final claim is covered/routine from prior exact structure even though the particular formula package was not printed together.

final_claim: For every finite commutative chain ring with residue-field order \(q\) and nilpotency length \(\ell\), the standard zero-divisor graph is the valuation-layer threshold blow-up; its automorphism group is the product of the layer symmetric groups, both determining number and metric dimension are \(q^{\ell-1}-\ell\), and the graph is determined by \((q,\ell)\).
scientific_limitations: The mathematics is correct, but the arbitrary-chain-ring layer structure is prior and the remaining invariants are routine consequences.
